_note: A8 backtest cases. Every event below is transcribed from the Research->Build handoff in D/Backtest_Candidates_for_Rai.md (14 Aug 2026) — its timeline, its dates, its source URLs. Nothing here is researched, inferred or extrapolated by the engine: an event the handoff does not date does not appear. Events on/after a case's `cutoff_date` are OUTCOMES, kept out of `events` so the lookback cannot see them; the harness asserts that separately.

cases.esg_score_basis: Mocked median baseline, 50 on the 0-100 scale. A backtest case is scored ALONE, so its percentile is 0.5 whatever this number is — writing it down makes explicit what the case notes already assert (see topglove: "negative momentum against a median-or-better baseline"). cases.profile: Emerging winner — transition milestones before recognition
cases.outcome: Completes the world's first market-based Energy Transition Mechanism: P7.2bn deal retiring the 246 MW SLTEC coal plant by 2040 instead of 2057
cases.caveats: No dated MSCI/Sustainalytics action is verifiable — recognition here is deal 'firsts', not rating moves. The ETM is debated (the plant still runs to 2040) and Ayala ownership complicates attribution.

cases.profile: The money case — a stable score masked deterioration
cases.outcome: US Customs and Border Protection issues a Withhold Release Order; formal forced-labour Finding follows in Mar 2021, RM3.6bn revenue lost — while the company was retained on the Dow Jones Sustainability Index for a third straight year in Nov 2021
cases.caveats: Low factual risk: the warning signals sit squarely inside the pre-Jul-2020 window, the outcome is a US government record, and the incumbent-score failure (DJSI retention through the episode) is documented.

events.text: Guardian investigation links its factories to forced labour indicators, including recruitment fees and debt bondage; the company's own rebuttal confirms the article
Continuing NGO and media reports on recruitment fees and debt bondage across its workforce
Further forced labour allegations over worker welfare and dormitory conditions remain unresolved

expect.label: overrated_leaders
expect.note: THE case. Dated forced-labour evidence sits inside the lookback while the incumbent score stayed stable — negative momentum against a median-or-better baseline is exactly the new `overrated_leaders` quadrant, and never Hidden Winners (signed disagreement forbids it).

cases.profile: The mandatory wrong case — where a naive momentum engine gets fooled
cases.outcome: DBS, OCBC and Standard Chartered decline or withdraw financing over the coal reality; Jun 2023 Mongabay reports the smelter will run on 2.2 GW of new captive coal to at least 2030 (~5.2 Mt CO2e/yr); Dec 2024 thermal-coal spin-off is itself called greenwashing
cases.caveats: The company contests the greenwashing label; no dated rating action is verifiable; the exact smelter announcement date (Dec 2021 vs early 2022) is unconfirmed. The rename/spin-off is a live entity-resolution hazard.

events.text: Announces a US$2bn aluminium smelter in a green industrial park, to be powered by planned renewable capacity
Adaro Green branding positions the group in the EV supply chain and clean energy transition narrative

expect.label: future_leaders
expect.note: PUBLISHED FAILURE CASE. Announcement-flow momentum at Feb 2023 was positive and the outcome was financing rejection — the engine is wrong here BY DESIGN of the data available at the cutoff. The mitigations are visible in the numbers, not in a caveat: both signals are company PR (quality capped at 0.5) and both use forward-looking language (materiality halved), so the engine's confidence stays low. The fix is source diversity, not a bigger weight.
